data.title: LatAm currencies mixed as tight Brazil elections keep investors on edge
data.description:
Key points:
  • IMF urges LatAm to cut debt, lift productivity while tailwinds last
  • Bolsonaro's lead over Lula narrows, polls this week show
  • World Bank sees up to $5 billion in possible loans to Venezuela, report says

By Sudeshna Ghoshal and Johann M Cherian

Latin American currencies were mixed on Friday, with Brazil in focus as new polls showed both presidential candidates in a tight race, while investors also assessed index operator MSCI's warnings about Indonesia's and Turkey's status as "emerging markets".

New polls this week showed the lead achieved by right-wing candidate Senator Flávio Bolsonaro during the first-round vote appeared to be dwindling into a technical tie with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, ahead of the presidential elections on October 25. The latest was a survey by CNT/MDA.

The real rose 0.42%, rebounding from a near-two week low, and was last trading at 5.0751 per dollar, while the Bovespa index managed a 0.4% gain.

However, both the assets were on course for weekly declines, with the currency and the equities benchmark set for their biggest weekly drop since mid-August.

Analysts also noted the significance of the government passing legislation that would reduce the country's workweek from six days to five.

"The passing of the labor reform, shortening the workweek, seems like a pro-Lula win even though plenty on the right agreed to also pass it," said Juan Perez, director of trading at Monex.

The elections are being closely watched by the US and China, given Brazil is the largest economy in Latin America at a time when the region has broadly seen a right-wing sweep in governments.

"There is growing concern about a political crisis potentially forming as Brazil navigates two diplomatic policies: holding firm with China and keeping the US as a friend," Perez said.

Data showed economic activity in Brazil rose by a seasonally adjusted 0.3% in August from the previous month, matching the median forecast in a Reuters poll of economists.

SELLOFFS IN TURKEY, INDONESIA

Turkey and Indonesia were under scrutiny after index provider MSCI warned of downgrades from "emerging market" status, citing a lack of transparency over trading practices.

Turkish equities fell nearly 3%, while Indonesian stocks tanked 11.6% and logged their biggest daily drop since 1998.

More broadly, MSCI's LatAm currency index (.MILA00000CUS) shed 0.4%, with declines led by Mexico's peso , which slipped 0.5%, and Chile's peso , which dipped 0.4%.

Mexico's equities benchmark gained 1.6%, with FEMSA up 6.1% after JP Morgan raised its rating on the bottler and retailer's shares in New York.

Stalled progress on the US-Mexico-Canada free trade deal remains a key overhang for the country.

Against this backdrop, the International Monetary Fund urged Latin American governments to take advantage of still-favorable global conditions to cut public debt and raise productivity, while warning that a fiscal adjustment has stalled in many countries including Mexico, Brazil and Colombia.

The World Bank said it sees up to $5 billion in possible loans to Venezuela over the next two years, a report said.

data.title: Omeros Shares Slide After CHMP Upholds Negative Opinion On Drug; Analyst Sees Buying Opportunity At $16
data.description:
Key points:
  • H.C. Wainwright views the weakness following the morning’s negative Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use opinion as overdone and sees a buying opportunity ahead of the next quarterly update.
  • Today’s decision, H.C. Wainwright said, does not change its forecasts, valuation, or investment thesis, while reiterating a Buy rating with a $33 price target.
  • The company now plans to license commercialization rights to a third party in the European Union (EU) if EU marketing authorization is granted.

Shares of Omeros Corp (OMER) slumped 15% on Friday after a European Medicines Agency committee upheld a negative opinion on its drug for a serious post-transplant condition, though H.C. Wainwright dismissed the selloff as overdone.

The stock is now on track for its steepest one-day decline since late June.

What Did The Analyst Say?

H.C. Wainwright views the weakness following the morning’s negative Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use opinion as overdone and sees a buying opportunity ahead of the next quarterly update. The firm said it had already removed Europe entirely from its model when it lowered its price target to $33 in June after the committee's initial negative opinion.

Today’s decision, H.C. Wainwright said, does not change its forecasts, valuation, or investment thesis, while reiterating a Buy rating with a $33 price target. The price target still implies a potential upside of about 100% from the stock’s current trading levels around $16.

Second European Rejection For Yartemlea

The Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) of the European Medicines Agency issued a negative opinion on Omeros’ marketing authorization application for narsoplimab, sold as Yartemlea in the United States, the company said on Friday. This followed a re-examination of the committee’s original negative decision from June.

An eight-member ad hoc expert group recommended that outside experts examine individual patient data to better understand factors linked to treatment response and survival, the company said. Omeros said it had submitted substantial patient-level data in August, but the CHMP did not share those records with the expert panel.

US Approval Stands In Contrast

Narsoplimab targets a rare and potentially fatal complication called hematopoietic stem cell transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy (TA-TMA), which damages small blood vessels after stem cell transplants. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved it in December 2025 as the first and only treatment for the condition in patients aged two and older. No approved therapy exists for TA-TMA in Europe.

“We are deeply disappointed in the re-examination process and outcome,” said Omeros CEO Gregory A. Demopulos.

The company also said that it will terminate the compassionate use program for the drug in the EU and focus on its U.S. market. Current patients will receive enough supply to finish treatment, Omeros added.

The company now plans to license commercialization rights to a third party in the European Union (EU) if EU marketing authorization is granted.

How Did OMER Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around OMER stock stayed within the bearish territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume rose from normal to high levels.

A Stocktwits user noted that the company has a partnership in place with Danish drugmaker Novo Nordisk for another drug called zaltenibart, which will eventually bring in milestone payments.

data.title: DraftKings Stock Whipsaws on NBA's Betting Crackdown — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Nick Devor

The National Basketball Association and its sports betting partners are banning certain bets this season, after prominent gambling scandals rocked the world of basketball last year.

Shares of DraftKings and FanDuel's parent company, Flutter, dropped on the news before recovering somewhat. Flutter shares were flat in afternoon trading; DraftKings was down 3%.

Some of the now-restricted bets were often tied together to form parlay bets, a bread-and-butter sportsbook product. Parlays link multiple individual wagers into one bet with a massive payout if each prediction proves correct. Their inherent long odds make parlays engaging for bettors and high-margin for sports betting operators.

The prohibited bets were outlined in a memo, reviewed by Barron's, sent to sports betting operators on Friday.

Bets being discontinued by the sportsbooks are those most susceptible to manipulation, such as "unders" on players expected to play less than 12 minutes a game. A customer might, for example, wager that a player will grab "under" eight rebounds in a game.

Those bets have featured prominently in alleged match-fixing scandals. Players intentionally scored fewer points or made fewer rebounds than normal in coordination with bettors who wagered that those players would underperform, according to law-enforcement officials. Defendants, including former Miami Heat point guard Terry Rozier, have pleaded not guilty.

Bets on which player will be the first to score a point or which team will win the starting tipoff are also prohibited going forward.

The new restrictions were the product of a collaboration between the league and its sportsbook partners, DraftKings, FanDuel, and Fanatics, according to an NBA spokesperson. They'll apply to all sports betting operators that use league data — but not prediction market platforms.

Prediction markets offer financial contracts that pay out on the outcome of sporting events, effectively enabling sports betting nationwide without abiding by the state regulations that govern traditional sportsbooks.

The NBA would like to see prediction markets adopt similar restrictions, the league spokesperson says, but they don't have commercial relationships with any prediction markets at this time and therefore lack the leverage to make those changes happen.

The league sent a second memo on Friday, also reviewed by Barron's, to the leadership of every NBA team outlining "improvements we have made to the league's sports betting integrity and compliance infrastructure."

The NBA has adopted artificial-intelligence tools to monitor unusual betting activity, and has updated its code of conduct for fans to add harsher penalties for "betting-related player harassment." Additionally, all players and team personnel will be required to attend an in-person training session detailing the league's sports betting rules.

data.title: CoreWeave Stock Slump Deepens — WSJ
data.description:
By Robbie Whelan

CoreWeave stock is having another tough day, bringing its weekly decline to 25%.

Part of the problem for the company is that it relies primarily on debt to finance its data centers and the Nvidia chips it installs in them. As of June, the cloud company's unsecured notes had a "B" rating from S&P Global Ratings, putting them solidly in junk territory. In its most recent quarterly filing, CoreWeave listed $35.6 billion in total debt on its balance sheet, plus billions more in lease obligations with data center landlords.

"They kind of represent the subprime tranche of the AI trade," said Gil Luria, a tech analyst at D.A. Davidson who has been critical of CoreWeave's debt-fueled business model.

Luria points to the company's most recent results, which included adjusted operating income of $128 million for the quarter, which implies $512 million in annual adjusted income. He compares that figure to CoreWeave's $46.7 billion in net assets in property and equipment, a figure that represented how much capital the company has invested in AI infrastructure.

Taken together, the two numbers imply a 1% return on invested capital. Given that CoreWeave is borrowing at interest rates of 9% or higher to finance its investments, income would have to improve dramatically for banks to remain comfortable lending to CoreWeave, Luria argues.

data.title: Trump move to restart direct US flights with Lebanon hits roadblock
data.description:
Key points:
  • UN regulator report finds safety issues at Beirut airport
  • Findings may hamper Trump's plan to resume US-Lebanon flights
  • Lebanon says corrective action being taken, progress delayed by war

By Allison Lampert and David Shepardson

The United Nations aviation agency has found Lebanon's main airport lacks valid certification, according to a report summary seen by Reuters, in a setback to US President Donald Trump's move to revive direct US-Beirut flights.

Trump made the announcement in July and signed an order last month for the US government to allow direct flights from the US to Lebanon, reversing a four-decade-long suspension after TWA Flight 847 was hijacked and forced to land in Beirut in 1985.

While the US Federal Aviation Administration and the Transportation Security Administration would still need to conduct safety reviews before flights could resume, the Lebanese embassy in Washington called Trump's order "a significant first step toward restoring direct air service between Lebanon and the United States."

However, the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) technical assistance mission to Lebanon in July identified shortcomings at Beirut-Rafic Hariri International Airport and in the aviation system.

The findings, which two senior industry officials familiar with the matter expect to delay the resumption of service, complicate efforts to follow up on an order Trump signed after meeting Lebanese President Joseph Aoun. Washington has backed Aoun as it pushes for Iran-backed Hezbollah to be disarmed.

The agency sent its internal report, made at the request of the Lebanese Civil Aviation Authority (LCAA), to Lebanon in September.

AIRPORT LACKS EMERGENCY PLAN: ICAO

Beirut airport's firefighting resources are equipped for single-aisle planes, but not twin-aisle jetliners used for long-haul flights, according to a summary of ICAO's report. The airport also lacks an emergency plan, and its conditional certification has expired, the report said.

"This is a serious and time-critical matter that must be addressed immediately to preserve the airport's operational status," the summary said.

The report also found the Lebanese regulator LCAA lacks qualified inspectors to oversee air traffic control licensing, and has no fully established, operational and independent aircraft accident investigation authority with clearly defined roles.

Such concerns were flagged during a two-day workshop last month where officials from ICAO, Lebanon's government, the FAA and others discussed efforts to revive direct air service, according to the industry officials and an agenda of the meeting seen by Reuters.

Lebanon's Minister of Public Works and Transport Fayez Rasamny said Lebanon was taking steps to address the concerns, with efforts to certify the airport starting on Saturday. The LCAA expects to issue conditional certification in the coming days.

"Most of the issues highlighted in the report had already been identified by the LCAA, and corrective action had already been initiated," Rasamny said in a statement, adding that progress had been delayed by war. Israeli forces remain in southern Lebanon and have continued strikes despite a US-brokered framework agreement signed in June between Israel and Lebanon. Hezbollah, which was not party to the deal, has rejected it.

The FAA declined to comment. ICAO said it cannot comment on matters concerning specific countries, but said it conducts targeted analyses for member states.

The US State Department advises Americans not to travel to Lebanon given safety concerns. It said the FAA advises caution for flights operating in Lebanese airspace due to heightened military activity in or around Syria, including the risks of errant long-range surface-to-air missiles originating from Syrian territory.

MIDDLE EAST UNREST DISRUPTS AIR TRAVEL

Foreign airlines have avoided large swathes of Middle East airspace because of missile and drone threats since US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February triggered regional hostilities, with an airport in Saudi Arabia the latest site to come under attack.

Lebanon and its national carrier have been praised domestically for maintaining air navigation services and flights, helping to prop up an economy that depends on tourism and remittances.

Three US airline officials told Reuters on the condition of anonymity they do not think any American carriers would resume flights to Lebanon in the near term, citing security concerns.

While there are no direct flights between Beirut and the United States, such service exists between Lebanon and some large European cities.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency said it was aware of the ICAO report and added that EU airlines must conduct their own assessment of an airport's safety and operational readiness before launching services.

data.title: FDA Drug Approvals In September 2026
data.description:
LONDON (dpa-AFX) - The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved 13 drugs in September 2026, spanning first-in-class therapies, treatments for rare diseases, and new options for patients with serious conditions.

With the month yielding a mix of new therapies and expanded treatment options, let's take a closer look at the drugs approved, the conditions they target, and the key pricing details behind them.

<u>1. Zanvastro (Zilganersen)</u>

Developed by: Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (IONS)

Approved on: September 3, 2026

Indication: Alexander disease

Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare, progressive, and ultimately fatal neurological disorder that affects one in every 1 to 3 million individuals. The disorder attacks patients' astrocytes, which support neurons in the brain, by introducing variations in the GFAP genes. The disease currently has no cure.

<I>Zanvastro </I>(zilganersen) is an antisense, oligonucleotide RNA- targeting therapy. The drug inhibits excess production of the glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), to restore the function of astrocytes in patients of AxD. The drug was formulated as an intrathecal solution.

The drug was granted a Breakthrough Therapy and Rare Pediatric Disease designations by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), in addition to an Orphan Drug designation from both the FDA and European Medicines Agency (EMA).

Positive data from the Phase 3 pivotal study for zilganersen in AxD was reported by the company. The trial assessed 49 pediatric and adult patients of AxD, who showed difficulty walking at baseline. Following treatment, patients demonstrated a meaningful stabilization of gait speed as measured by the 10 metre walk test (10MWT), showcasing improvements in gross motor function at week 61.

Ionis previously announced entering a license agreement with Recordati for the international commercialization of Zilganersen in treating Alexander disease. The drug is now the first and only treatment for AxD.

According to the company, <I>Zanvastro </I>will be available at a wholesale acquisition cost (WAC) of $285,000 per dose.

Stock Quote: IONS has been trading in a range of $42.08 ?to $86.74 in the last 1 year. The stock closed yesterday's trading at $44.12, up 3.33%.

<u>2. Omcazio (cabozantinib)</u>

Developed by: Handa Pharmaceuticals Inc. (6620.TWO)

Approved on: September 3, 2026

Indication: Carcinoma of the kidney and liver, extra-pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors

Carcinomas arise from epithelial tissues of various organs and are the most common forms of malignancies, accounting for 80% to 90% of all cancer diagnoses.

Neuroendocrine tumors, however, originate from cells that regulate hormone release, and can impair signaling between nerve cells as well.

<I>Omcazio </I>is a laurylsulfate salt formulation of the kinase inhibitor cabozantinib, which has previously been approved in other formulations for treating cancers of the thyroid, kidney, liver and pancreas. In this most recently approved composition, Omcazio can be used to treat renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in adults as a monotherapy or in combination with nivolumab.

Additionally, it may be utilized to treat hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in adults who have received prior treatment with sorafenib. It is also approved for adult and pediatric patients with previously treated, unresectable, advanced, or metastatic extra-pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (epNET).

The drug is to be offered in doses of 34.5 mg, 23 mg, and 11.5 mg.

<I>CABOMETYX</I>, developed by Exelixis, is the original approved formulation of cabozantinib that generated a U.S. revenue of $2.11 billion in 2025.

data.title: Dividend delight on D-Street: Modison, LTM to Oberoi Realty announce dividends on October 16 | Amount, record dates
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- Dividend delight on D-Street: As the September quarter earnings season has kicked off in full swing, nearly three companies announced dividends on Friday, October 16. Modison Limited, LTM Limited, and Oberoi Realty Limited rewarded investors with cash payouts.

All the three firms have fixed Friday, October 23 as the record date. For dividend hunters, here are all the details about these companies' dividend payouts, record date, and most importantly Q2FY27 results.

Modison Limited, on Friday, declared a 400% dividend for the financial year 2026-27. The company's board of directors has approved Rs.4 dividend per equity share with a face value of Re 1 each.

The company has fixed Friday, October 23, as the record date to determine the eligibility of shareholders for the payout.

Modison's net profit stood at Rs.2,332.3 lakhs in Q2FY 27 against a net profit of Rs.1,165.69 lakh reported in the year-ago period. Its net revenue from operations increased to Rs.27,902.59 lakhs in Q2FY27 against Rs.14,516.21 lakhs reported in the year ago period. Its net revenue stood at Rs.27,046.67 lakh in Q1FY27.

Oberoi Realty's board of directors approved a second interim dividend for FY26-27 at the rate of Rs.2 per equity share, i.e. 20% of the face value of Rs.10 each. Investors must own the stock before the record date to qualify for the payout. The board has fixed Friday, October 23, as the record date to determine eligibility of shareholders for the payout.

Its net consolidated profit increased marginally to Rs.761.65 crore for the quarter ended September, a marginal increase from the year-ago period. Its net profit stood at Rs760.26 crore in the year-ago period.

data.title: Arabica coffee touches one-month high as stocks remain critically low
data.description:
Arabica coffee futures on ICE rallied to a one-month high on Friday as market participants grew nervous that critically low exchange stocks will not be replenished as soon as previously expected.

COFFEE

* Arabica coffee settled up 10.8 cents, or 3.7%, at $3.056 per lb​​. It earlier hit a one-month high of $3.1130.

* ICE-certified stocks were last at 238,976 bags, not far off last month's 27-year-low of 217,646 bags.

* Market participants are growing nervous that supplies from top grower Brazil will not arrive at ICE warehouses ahead of the December contract expiry, leaving stocks critically low, dealers said.

* Coffee is also being boosted by concerns that the El Nino weather event will curb top grower Brazil's output next year, and by the recent strength of Brazil's real currency .

* Robusta coffee settled up $41, or 1.2%, at $3,405 a ton.

* The harvest in top grower Vietnam is getting underway and industry participants expect output will be roughly steady versus last year, though El Nino conditions are set to hurt the 2027/28 crop.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​settled down £134, or 3%, at £4,356 per ton, after setting a 1-1/2-month high of £4,640 on Wednesday.

* Cocoa grind data in key processing regions around the world rose a greater-than-expected 14.3% in the third quarter as demand recovered further from the 2025 slump, data showed.

* "It seems that demand for cocoa has recovered from the slump that followed the massive price rise in 2024," said Commerzbank.

* New York cocoa ​​settled down $186, or 3.2%, at $5,645 a ton, having set a one-month peak on Wednesday.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar fell 0.28 cents, or 1.3%, to 20.85 cents per lb​​, having hit a 19-month peak of 21.29 on Wednesday.

* Sugar is being driven by excess El Nino-linked rains in top grower Brazil, which slowed production in September and reduced the sucrose in the cane.

* Brazil said on Wednesday sugar production in its center-south region fell 6% in the second half of September to 2.86 million tons.

* Europe, meanwhile, suffered a severe drought this summer that damaged the beet crop, while No. 2 grower India has been hit by El Nino-linked dryness.

* White sugar fell $6.20, or 1.1%, to $554.90 a ton.

data.title: Wheat Futures Fall as Grains Limp Into Weekend — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Kirk Maltais

-Wheat for December delivery fell 1.5% to $6.59 3/4 a bushel on the Chicago Board of Trade Friday, with the overall grains complex finishing off the week under pressure amid tough macro conditions and friendlier-than-expected weather in the Corn Belt.

-Corn for December delivery fell 0.8% to $4.74 1/4 a bushel.

-Soybeans for November delivery fell 0.2% to 12.60 1/2 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

On the Home Front: Grain futures have been trending lower this fall in part because of a change in how traders are viewing the weather in crop-growing regions around the world. "The weather story that helped fuel grain-market optimism is beginning to unravel," said Scott Mathews of BestWeather in a note. "Improving rainfall across the U.S. Plains, favorable early-season conditions in South America, and substantial speculative exposure could leave corn, soybeans, and wheat vulnerable to additional selling." For corn and soybeans, this ties to weather allowing farmers in their fields to harvest their crops, while for wheat it means being able to get into the fields to plant.

Cut and Run: There's speculation fund traders are pulling out of long positions in corn, said Charlie Sernatinger of Marex in a note. "[Corn is] down anticipating a weekend harvest prehedge tonight, more chart selling, and talk that macro funds are exiting commodities anticipating a U.S. recession," says Sernatinger. Last week's Commitments of Traders report from the CFTC showed a sizable decrease in long corn positions, with nearly 55,000 long contracts shown being closed. The CFTC will be updating its report this afternoon, although the data is a few days behind.

Feeling Flat: The USDA this week announced multiple export sales of U.S. soybeans to China, including a new flash sale of 558,000 tons announced today. An additional 236,000 tons of soybeans sold to "unknown destinations" were also reported. "Unknown destinations" is an alternative moniker that's often used for Chinese buyers, although not necessarily the case. But CBOT soybeans didn't respond by going higher, as China's return to buying U.S. soybeans was at least partially expected, said Joe Davis of Futures International in a note.

INSIGHT

Slack Showing: Grain futures closed out the week with a weak showing, continuing a skid that began last month. Corn settled lower for the fourth session in a row, according to FactSet data. Soybeans finished the week in the negative for the fifth session in a row, making it 7 out of the past 8 sessions it's closed down. Wheat finished lower for the 6th session out of the past 8. A stronger U.S. dollar and friendlier-than-expected weather in the Corn Belt has applied the pressure to the grains complex.

Farming for the Future: U.S. farmers are increasingly utilizing drones to spray their farmland, said the American Farm Bureau Federation in a note. The AFBF says that 16.4 million acres of farmland were sprayed by drones in 2025, up roughly five times from 3.7 million acres in 2023. The usage of drones is increasing as farmers see them as ways to handle problems with accessing certain portions of their fields. "The biggest advantages for drones come in wet fields, rough terrain, irregularly shaped fields and situations where timely product applications are critical," said Bernt Nelson of the AFBF.

AHEAD

-The USDA will release its weekly Grain Export Inspections report at 11 a.m. ET Monday.

-The USDA will release its weekly Crop Progress report at 4 p.m. ET Monday.

-The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10:30 a.m. ET Wednesday.
